sections.bio:
I build AI products and help founders raise capital. That's what I do. That's what I post about.
 
Co-founded Correcto, an AI writing tool. Raised $8M. Grew to 75,000 users in 6 months. Featured in Forbes, TechCrunch, and 100+ publications. Led a team of 20 across London, Madrid, and the US.
 
CMO at Ikualo: 40,000 downloads in 2.5 months for a fintech serving 23M underbanked Europeans. Ran paid media, social, and growth strategy from day one.
 
Helped founders raise over $15M in venture capital.
 
Now building an AI tool that runs your paid ads for you.
 
I post daily about: → AI marketing: what's working, what's not, what's next → Fundraising: real lessons from pre-seed to Series A → B2B growth: frameworks you can steal and use today
 
Building or raising? DM me.

Pulled from the shift already underway: marketers who open Claude Code operate a system. The ones who do not stay as fast as they are now.

What's inside:

1/ The old way, and why it is breaking
You open the chat app. It writes the post. You go post it. It runs the audit. You spend the afternoon doing it. It gives you the report. You pull the numbers yourself. The copy-paste is the work, and it is not your judgment, it is your labor.

2/ The new way
A version of Claude that does the work instead of describing it. Opens your files. Connects to your tools. Runs on a schedule while you sleep. Same intelligence. The only difference is whether you carry the work or it does.

3/ The 3 powers
Act in your real tools, not just write the email. Touch your real files, not just tell you the format. Run unattended on a schedule, not just respond when you ask. Each removes a different chunk of the manual work between you and the result.

4/ The setup that makes it run
The brain file that grounds every run in your business. The connectors that give it hands. The auto mode that runs the safe middle without babysitting. The schedule that makes it work while you sleep.

5/ The 3 builds in order
The foundation: where the work runs unattended. The first real workflow: a job you do by hand, taken off your hands. The plugins: new skills installed in one click. Each is a step up from doing the work to running a system.

6/ The forces making it inevitable
The chat app advises. Claude Code presses the buttons, with you deciding which. The gap between marketers who open the Code tab and the ones who never do is about to be the widest skill gap in the field.

7/ The first three moves to start now
Open the desktop app and the Code tab. Write your first CLAUDE.md in plain English. Run one workflow you currently do by hand and watch it run without you. Whatever size you are today.

The pattern in every build: the AI does the work, you keep the judgment. The honest part is in the guide, including why most marketers will not open Claude Code and what that does to the skill gap.

500+ funds, startups, and real estate sponsors in our first 60 days.

When we launched 8Raise, the bet was simple. Raising capital does not have to mean cold lists, dead inboxes, and guessing who actually writes checks. It should mean the right investors, the warm path, and a process that runs even when you step away from the desk.

Sixty days in, the founders, fund managers, and sponsors raising with 8Raise have told us the bet was right.

Here is what 500+ of them are now running on:

→ Three modes built for how capital actually moves: VC, Real Estate, and LP


To everyone who trusted us in the first 60 days: thank you. You did the hard part. We are just making the next 60 faster.

If you are raising a round, a fund, or a deal, this is the moment to assemble your stack.

From first outreach to funded.

🔗 www.8raise.com

Couple days ago, Jake Paul and Logan Paul closed an oversubscribed $100M growth fund.

Anti Fund, with Geoffrey Woo and Jake Paul as managing partners and Logan as GP, is now past $180M in AUM, just six months after its $30M Fund I.

The model is a barbell: small first checks into technical founders, then $10M+ growth checks into the ones that break out. Growth already holds OpenAI, Anduril, SpaceX, Cognition, and Helion.

The verticals tell you exactly where the money's headed:

→ AI
→ Defense
→ Robotics
→ Energy
→ Frontier infrastructure

Read it as a founder raising. Anti Fund's own thesis: capital is a commodity, attention is not. The Pauls didn't out-capital anyone. They turned reach into access, and access into a fund.

You don't need 20M followers to borrow that move. You need reach to the right investors before consensus gets there.

And that's the whole game we help founders run: not more capital, more access to the people who write the checks.

sections.title: Why work with me
sections.body:
I don't sell banner placements. Your product shows up inside the real fundraising and AI workflows I write about every week, which is why it converts instead of getting scrolled past.

The numbers:
- ~250 qualified calls booked per month for the products I promote
- ~35K average views per post, 5M+ LinkedIn impressions in 60 days
- Audience that holds budget: 39% Founder / C-level, 40% founders by function, plus Finance / VC and operators across the US, UK, and Europe

If you sell to founders raising capital or operators automating their work, this is the room you want to be in.

sections.title: What I offer
sections.body:
Single post: a fully integrated post in my voice, built around your product inside a real workflow.

One month (4 posts): a weekly run across the month so your product gets repeated exposure, not a one-off.

Cross-channel partnership: my co-founder Ignacio and I run a full month across both LinkedIn profiles plus our 8fundraising Substack: 8 posts, one full sponsored article, and natural mentions woven into the weekly issues. This is where the call-booking numbers come from. Priced and scheduled on a quick call.

Best fits: investor CRM and outreach tools, AI and automation products, pitch and data-room software, fundraising and cap-table platforms, fund admin tools.

sections.title: How I work
sections.body: You send a brief. I write the post in my own voice and slot it into the content calendar so it reads as editorial, not an ad. The post anchors a comment-to-DM CTA, which is what drives the high comment volume and routes interested people to a conversation. You get the qualified inbound, I keep editorial control so it lands.

sections.title: Time from booking to post
sections.body: Single posts: 5 to 7 business days from approved brief to live, so it's written properly and placed in the right slot. Monthly packages: scheduled across the month on confirmation.
